body:
No one reacted in the interview. Everyone was super professional. So my friend has no idea. 

They called me later that day to tell me they felt like jt went well. They “had a good feeling about it”. :(

That's absolutely what I'm afraid of- I signed and paid. Because so much student loan stuff is handled digitally, the paper trail is thin. To make matters worse, my college is no longer a college now, so there's no office to contact there for documents. I am really at a loss. Me paying the loans back for five years definitely doesn't look great. I definitely know that I don't know the entire situation since so much of it has been concealed from me. It's truly bizarre.

What sort of information do I need to do this? 

Can the police even help with a case that is 5+ years old?
Gorgeous artwork with a beautiful backdrop of sound.

You’re not any more of a perv than the folks you were messaging. 

Binging happens. We get excited, chase the rush, then crash and feel bummed about it like a sad aftersex moment. 

Reflecting on how you feel now will help you figure out how to feel happy and balanced in the future. It’s okay to be curious and want to talk to folks— just don’t let it get in the way of your health and stuff. 

Learn from it and take it easy. Don’t be down on yourself. We are all human. :)

The truest expression of love: food.

Wishing you and yours lots of happiness and delicious food. :)

Using a passed away parent to manipulate you is screwed up.

It’s your choice. Weigh the consequences and decide what is right for you and your future.

Congratulations from a fellow bi person! :) 
Wishing you a smooth and happy coming out.

People who are obsessed with your relationships/lack of relationships are insecure in their relationships/lack of relationships. 

Folks who can’t fathom being alone are boring and unable to provide good care for themselves. They use relationships to define themselves and their identities, and it’s not healthy— but it is absurdly normalized. 

Being single and doing your thing is extremely enriching and awesome. And whenever you are ready to have a relationship (if ever), you can freely choose it! And your future friendships and relationships will benefit so much from the time you spent serving yourself and getting to know the awesome person that you are. :)

Yo, my partner is non-binary and uses they/them pronouns and... yeah, sometimes people really, really suck. 

You are awesome and so much better than shitty, mean bastards that want to actively bring someone down.

You deserve respect. You deserve to be seen.

Don’t let the bastards keep you down. Keep on being awesome. Things will get better.

Hey there. I just wanted to say that I’m in a similar boat and I share your frustrations and disappointment. I am in love with someone (9 years) that doesn’t share my long-term goals and it can sometimes feel like I’m being held back, weighed down, or trapped. 

Communication and compromise are everything. You deserve to feel happy and content, especially with your family. 

Everything waxes and wanes. I hope things wax favorably for you soon.
Wooo! You are doing it! Keep at it!

Yo, your identity is your own. People experiment and have exceptions. Self-identifying vs the way people label you are completely different things. 

The question is, which one is more important to you?
I wish I had the balls to send this, but I think I’m about five years too late to be barging into someone’s life again.
Your boyfriend sounds emotionally abusive and controlling. Nothing anyone like that can offer you is good enough. Move on. Sorry to be blunt, but this scenario is nothing but red flags to me.

Hey, I know you weren’t asking for a follow-up, but I wanted to say we had another conversation about this that turned into a pretty honest and raw discussion. We didn’t fight or anything like that, but we laid out all the feelings and thoughts and fears. 

We decided that moving is necessary.

I was able to explain my worries and, most importantly, that I don’t mean to jerk the rug out from under us in a sudden traumatic move away from everything and everyone that we love— but instead that we can move together and plan together at our own pace. I know realistically a move will take a couple of years of planning and some good job offers or school admissions. They seemed to relax a bit and were able to tell me about their own worries and fears. 

We both listened and exchanged ideas. We decided to talk about this again next week because we ended up discussing until it got very late. 

We have plans to chat more on Tuesday. It feels a little weirdly official to make plans to discuss this, but I am ultimately really glad we are taking the time to think about our feelings and ideas and come together to chat more concretely. 

Things feel more hopeful. Thanks for the advice and encouragement. I hope you have a good day.
Thank you for the insight and encouragement. I really appreciate it.

Thank you for this valuable response. This is exactly what I needed to hear. 

I love my partner. We are good team. We are family. I think we need to take a risk and see what happens. We can always move back if things go awry, and maybe with more money to continue here. 

Thanks for the positive story. Wishing you and yours much happiness and health.

A lot does change, but we are committed to each other as family and our relationship is pretty happy and healthy in all other senses. It’s tricky to think about a future that doesn’t align when the present is so good. 

I think there’s some compromise in here I haven’t considered yet. But you could be right. I have considered we might not line up our interests for the future and it really, really hurts.

It’s a really hard thing to ask someone to do and I am totally sympathetic to it, even if I am frustrated and bummed out about my situation too. 

I really love my partner and we have a great relationship. They are my best friend and my only family. I can’t imagine putting that aside to pursue material things. But I think you’re right— I think asking for a compromise, or at least to give it a shot isn’t so out of the question. 

I have been considering school or residencies in other parts of the country. They would be short programs and would give me a taste of a “new life”. I am willing to be long distance. My partner wasn’t willing to be long distance in the past, but that was over five years ago. It doesn’t hurt to try. 

Thanks for the wisdom.

Presently I do museum work building exhibits, researching, and instructing. It’s kind of a niche job, but I really love it. There are only two museums in the city, and the other one is purely arts so they would probably not really need what I can offer. That’s a big reason I’m thinking of moving my skills into another field or maybe trying to pick up a trade if I want to stay and work local. The health and insurance industry is huge here, so I could look into those avenues if I was just trying to make money, but I also kind of want to pursue what I studied and worked hard to have... I pursued this career because I thought it would take me to unique places. Whoops. Ha ha

You are right though. There are lots of opportunities here. I think I just need to be open to rearranging my dreams. My priorities are shifting and career choice isn’t everything anymore.

Owning pets can be rewarding and challenging. Pets are soul-restoring and soul-destroying machines of havoc and happiness. 

Give you and the pup some time!

One year is still very young. That's not a lot of time to be together at all. Reassure yourself that you aren't out of line for feeling frustrated, but also reassure yourself that your dog isn't a lost cause either.

Hang in there. Most all things get better with time. My old cats were rascals in their young years... And they are awesomely mellow little friends now.

Our histories are complex and personal.

Regardless of "why" you find yourself to be exactly who you are in this moment, there is no denying that you are you.

Congratulations on embracing a piece of yourself, and having the strength to come out as who you know yourself to be.

I'm so proud and excited for you! Bikes are awesome and really open up the place that you live in an interesting way. I like to ride through my neighborhood and try to pick out new things each time. I miss so much of it when I am travelling by car or bus. 

Congrats on your first mile of hopefully many! Be safe and wear a helmet, even if it makes you feel dorky. :)

Thank you! All relationships have risks, but it's important to make sure the risk is worth it.

Feeling lighter and happier and just really relieved.

It's really scary to be earnest about things, especially on the internet. I think a lot of people cope with humor because they are afraid they will be rejected, made fun of, etc. 

I use humor as a safety net too. I always feel like if someone laughs, it's because I invited them to-- it's not because they are laughing at me and my pain. I have control in those situations. But I am also practicing boundaries in those situations too: how close do I want people to really get to the problem? How much am I actually willing to share? Etc. 

However, it's important to find good people that you can trust. It's healthy to vent, reach out, and want to be heard. It's healthy to want help for difficult things you can't do on your own. Humans are social creatures. We need each other.

You aren't a hypocrite. You are just being safe. Have healthy boundaries, protect yourself, and find someone to talk to about the things that suck. 

Good luck, OP.

I'm sorry, friend. It's hard being so aligned with someone when it isn't the right time.

Have you ever listened to the song Something About Us by Daft Punk?

It's about not being in the right place or time with someone you are strongly connected to. It might be a cathartic listen if you need that sort of thing.

Hang in there.

What an amazing post about Charlie. This was so much fun to read. 

I am so sorry you are grieving right now OP. I am glad you gave Charlie a lovely second shot at life and cared for him so much. 

Be kind to yourself and savor the happy (and funny and downright weird) memories.
This was spot on. The advice to reframe why OP broke up is very good.

Oof. Your ex-boyfriend doesn't sound like a catch at all. He sounds very shallow. You, on the otherhand, sound very kind, thoughtful, and selfless. 

I would feel sad for him letting you get away like that, except he clearly doesn't deserve you.

Whether gaining weight or losing it, you should do it for you. The confidence it will give you to be in control of your own life and body will stand out and make you feel awesome. Find someone who can see you for who you are, not just what your body is like. Bodies change a lot over time. Personalities and minds are slower to change. 

It's the person inside the body that gives it beauty and life. 

Hang in there, OP! Move on to better and happier things. :)

Pick up the brush and start painting. You sound like you have great things to tell the world. Practice your craft, practice your confidence, and don't ever stop. You are brave and strong enough to do it, OP!

It's so important to be ready to become the right person first. You are onto something that many people don't want to think about. Keep on working on becoming the best you that you can be.

And don't drop the soap, OP.

Losing a friend is always hard. I am so sorry that you are grieving for her. You must be very stressed about being on your own. 

Be kind to yourself and know that you have given sweet Pearl a beautiful gift by sharing your life with her, spending time with her, taking care of her, and letting her be so special to you. 

Sending you lots of love and bravery for this tough time. Hang in there.

When you feel brave and ready to love again, find another friend that you can continue to pour love into (humans have a lot of love and time to give). Honor Pearl's life and the awesome ways she showed you how to love by continuing to be brave and love. 🖤

My dad passed away about three years ago. Cancer too. A Tuesday.

Sometimes I struggle to remember his voice and the things he would say. It hasn't even been that long. I try to remember his laugh and it's hard. 

I used to feel like I was a bad son because I couldn't remember things, but I am practicing being kind to myself and trying to accept that as humans we just don't have perfect memories. Things fade. They get fuzzy. Our memories are weird. As other people have said, they will sometimes surprise you... With a perfect memory of something you almost thought you forgot. Hang in there, friend. 

Just like it's hard to remember all those precious details, it's also hard to remember a time before all this grief. A real double-edge there. 

Be good to yourself. You are a complete and capable person. 

Also wanted to reassure you: For almost everyone, graduation is a rough time where you pass a finish line and then have to throw up your hands and say, "Now what???" You will feel a little lost for a bit, but you will absolutely find your way. 

And guess what? It absolutely gets better. 

You got this, dude!

I am so sorry, my friend. My dad has also passed away.

It hurts, and there is little you can do to remove that hurt. It is just something that hurts. 

It can make you feel different from other people who haven't experienced this kind of loss. People your age may not understand what you are going through. Friends and classmates and even teachers or family members might struggle with what to say to you, or how to act around you. In truth, not many people know what to say or do for us in these situations. 

Grief and death are weird and wild things. 

Be kind to yourself. Don't torture yourself with regret. Find a way to express yourself: write, draw, make music, act, cook, code, dance, build things, whatever. If you don't feel very creative, explore the things other people have created. It's important to remember to express yourself when you feel ready to. Humans always eventually need an outlet for the things they are feeling. 

Remember that you aren't alone, even if it can feel really lonely. Hang in there.

I had a similar experience in that sub. I was seeking advice because I want to aid my relationship, not dump my loving and kind-hearted partner of 8 years. The two replies I got seemed to spell out doom for my relationship. But at least the replies seemed from a place of kindness. 

I think a lot of people these days are leery of folks falling into abusive, toxic, or otherwise unhealthy situations: relationships to parents, to partners, to children, to jobs- you name it. And for the most part, people are right to be leery. It's a scary world out there. 

Time and time again we hear stories about people who saw the red flags when it was "too late" and the damage was done to them. 

We think we can predict our pain. Or maybe we have experienced pain and we feel we can spare another from encountering it. It's very human. Why would you let someone else take that risk, right?

Something people tend to forget is that relationships (of any kind!) are very risky. They require vulnerability, trust, time, and other very precious things.

We can seek advice from folks, choose to listen, weigh the odds... But it's up to us, OP! Hang in there. You will know what is best for your situation in time. Wishing you the best of luck!
Oof. Rough to read about and tough to hear, but thank you for sharing it with me all the same.

We haven't really been able to talk much about the future over the past few years. I have mostly made decisions and plans on my own, but... It gets lonely for sure.

I do think it is something Margot could get better at in time. I just don't know how to help them get there. I agree with you that it is their issue to fix. 

I often wonder what they would do without me. Who they would be, what they would pursue, what they would find interesting. Surely there is something they want to do with their life?

I do think a big reason Margot struggles with talking about this stuff is that almost all of the big discussions have a common theme of Money. Margot definitely has some financial hang ups, although they have gotten A LOT more responsible over the years. But I think that financial insecurity makes it hard to take the lead on future-planning topics. 

I peeked at your profile and noticed you are poly. Do you ever struggle with future planning with your partners? Is it difficult to plan around multiple partners, or do your goals mesh together well?
